requirements.rationale:
1. Root cause: jira/issues.py line 104 currently reads
`if fields_param == "*all" or fields_set == DEFAULT_READ_JIRA_FIELDS:` and falls
through to `list(DEFAULT_READ_JIRA_FIELDS)` at line 109 — treating '*all' as
identical to "use defaults". The fix must separate the '*all' branch so it requests
the issue's full field catalog instead.
requirements.title: The jira_get_issue tool shall return every populated field, including custom fields, when called with fields='*all', rather than substituting the default field set

vision.section: §5 — Goals & Success Criteria (MVP), Goal 1: Fix the `*all` formatter contract violation
vision.paraphrase: The `jira_get_issue` tool's documented behavior for `fields='*all'` must match its implementation — returning the complete field catalog including custom fields rather than silently falling back to a subset.

conops.paraphrase: When a caller explicitly requests every field via `*all`, the method must separate its handling from the default-field path so custom fields are included in the response.

requirements.title: The jira_get_issue tool shall return exactly the fields named in an explicit, non-'*all' fields parameter, unaffected by the '*all'-handling fix

vision.section: §5 — Goals & Success Criteria (MVP), Cross-cutting Concerns: Surgical, minimal diffs
vision.paraphrase: The fix to the `*all` branch must not affect behavior for callers with explicit field names; the changes must be narrowly scoped to prevent unintended regressions.

conops.paraphrase: When a caller requests specific named fields, the implementation must honor that request exactly, without interference from the `*all` fix logic.

requirements.title: The jira_get_issue tool shall return a well-formed '*all' response, with no error, for an issue with no populated custom fields beyond the standard set

vision.section: §5 — Goals & Success Criteria (MVP), Cross-cutting Concerns: Backward compatible by default
vision.paraphrase: The `*all` fix must handle issues with no custom fields gracefully, ensuring that existing callers using `*all` on simple issues continue to work without errors.

conops.paraphrase: The fixed method must handle edge cases where no custom fields exist, returning a valid response that preserves the contract of the documented behavior.

requirements.rationale:
1. Root cause: models/jira/issue.py from_api_response() stores every customfield_*
key returned by the Jira API (including null values) in self.custom_fields.
to_simplified_dict() for *all iterates all of them and emits {"value": None} dicts.
The final `{k: v for k, v in result.items() if v is not None}` filter does not
remove these because the wrapper dict itself is not None.
2. Jira returns all defined field keys (including nulls) when fields=*all is requested.
Instances with thousands of defined custom fields produce thousands of null entries in the
LLM response context without this filter.
requirements.title: The jira_get_issue tool shall exclude custom fields whose value is null or an empty list from '*all' responses, so that LLM context is not flooded with empty field entries on instances with many defined custom fields

vision.section: §5 — Goals & Success Criteria (MVP), Goal 2: Filter null custom fields from `*all` responses
vision.paraphrase: When `*all` is used, only custom fields with populated values should appear in the response, preventing null entries from consuming LLM context on instances with thousands of defined custom fields.

conops.paraphrase: After the Jira REST API returns all fields including nulls, the response processing must filter out custom fields with null or empty-list values before they reach the LLM context.

requirements.rationale:
1. An earlier iteration expanded DEFAULT_READ_JIRA_FIELDS to 18 fields (adding
issuelinks, subtasks, parent, components, fixVersions, attachment, resolution,
resolutiondate). After maintainer feedback and upstream reference review, that
approach was reversed. Callers needing relationship or custom field data should use
jira_search_fields to discover field IDs and pass them explicitly via the fields
parameter.
2. This TOR supersedes TOR-01-el7Cazx (removed), TOR-01-7XlRNfG (removed), and
TOR-01-NfGirOm (removed), which asserted the expanded 18-field set.
requirements.title: DEFAULT_READ_JIRA_FIELDS shall contain exactly the 10 essential fields from the upstream sooperset/mcp-atlassian project, with no additional fields, ensuring default responses remain aligned with the upstream contract

vision.section: §5 — Goals & Success Criteria (MVP), Goal 3: Align default field set with upstream
vision.paraphrase: The default field set must remain at the upstream's 10-field 'essential only' alignment; callers needing relationship or custom field data should use explicit field parameters rather than rely on a default expansion.

conops.paraphrase: The recommended pattern for an LLM assistant that needs relationship data is to use `jira_search_fields` to discover field IDs first, then request them explicitly via the fields parameter, keeping the default set lightweight and predictable.
